heard: In 1907, inspectors measured a bending steel cord on the Quebec Bridge. Designing engineer Peter Schlapka drafted the lower cords with a defective design. Consulting engineer Theodore Cooper officially approved these flawed plans. Officials placed complete confidence in Cooper's judgment. But contemporary professional knowledge of steel columns under load was inadequate. By August 27, no action could prevent the structural collapse. – yet better judgment could have saved human lives on the site.
